tagline: An open-source agent for the models you run yourself
intro: OpenCLI is an agent that runs on your own computer and works with any OpenAI-compatible model — one on the machine in front of you, one on your own server, or a hosted provider when you want one. It reads your files, runs your commands and edits your work, in a terminal and in a desktop app that share the same conversations.
nothing_built_in: **Nothing is built in.** No models, no accounts, no keys, and no opinion about where your inference comes from. Point it at an endpoint and its models appear on their own; what you type goes there and nowhere else.
download_note: The app updates itself afterwards. These builds carry no Apple or Microsoft certificate, so the first launch needs one extra step
then_point: Then point it at a model.
f_files_t: Works on files, not just code.
f_files_b: It reads a folder of invoices the same way it reads a repository — and most of the work people actually have is the first kind.
f_office_b: A **department** is a directory with standing instructions. A **bot** is a chat inside one, with a job. Nine departments ship with sample data, so each can be tried before it is set up.
f_duty_t: Duties that come round on their own
f_duty_b: — and stop to ask you when they reach something they should not decide alone. That threshold is written in words, in advance: *any single line over 10,000*.
f_handoff_t: Bots hand work to each other,
f_handoff_b: with what they did and the files they produced. Capped at eight hops and three appearances each, so a cascade cannot run away.
f_skills_b: and work in any directory: reviewing rows against their rules, reporting what changed over a week, triaging an inbox, comparing two drafts, turning a transcript into decisions and owners, and reading records for what is worth checking.
f_connectors_b: — GitHub, Postgres, Slack, Notion, a browser. Keys are kept away from the configuration file, which gets shared.
f_sandbox_t: A sandbox with a visible edge.
f_sandbox_b: A run may write inside its own directory and nowhere else, and a run pointed somewhere unfamiliar is held until you allow that place by name.
f_languages_b: and any other is one JSON file you can add without rebuilding anything.
f_surfaces_t: Terminal, desktop and a local web UI
f_surfaces_b: over the same gateway, so a conversation started in one continues in another.
protocol_not_integrations: Not thirty integrations — one protocol. Anything answering `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/models` the way OpenAI does can be pointed at, and its models appear on their own. Every endpoint below was asked for its model list before being listed here.
g_closed: Closed models, when you want one
free_allowance: Several give a free allowance, which is the cheapest way to try a model larger than your machine can hold. Endpoints, and which providers carry which model:
reachable_t: Reachable is not the same as good at this.
reachable_b: Tool calling separates a model that can do this work from one that can only talk about it, and the model card never says.
check_note: one fixed task, five minutes. The table has one row because one model has been run, and **adding a row is the most useful contribution you can make.**
c_grep_t: General open models reach for `grep` when they have a file tool.
c_grep_b: A gap in the models; no interface closes it.
c_tokens_t: Token counts are estimated, never counted.
c_tokens_b: The tokenizer belongs to the model, and this runs models it has never seen.
c_schedule_t: Scheduled work runs only while OpenCLI is open.
c_schedule_b: A local agent, not a server.
c_sandbox_t: A background run may write anything inside the directory it runs in.
c_signing_t: The desktop builds are not signed.
c_signing_b: Your operating system is right to warn you.
c_rtl_t: Right-to-left languages are not laid out yet.
origin_1: A fork of [OpenAI's Codex CLI](https://github.com/openai/codex), Copyright 2025 OpenAI, Apache-2.0. **Not affiliated with OpenAI.**
origin_2: Codex is built for OpenAI's models and this is built for everybody else's, which changes more than a name. Departments, bots, duties, background runs and the workflows are ours, as is a good deal of work on what breaks when the model is small — a compaction loop that summarised once a turn for eleven turns and threw away the thread each time, and a token estimate that read a page of Chinese as three quarters of its real cost.
